planting.note: Direct sow or start indoors 4-6 weeks before last frost; bupleurum tolerates light frost and performs best as a cool-season crop, bolting and losing quality in sustained summer heat.

directions: Sow in well-drained, average garden soil in full sun, thinning to 6-9 inches apart; bupleurum is a florist's staple grown not for showy petals but for its airy sprays of tiny, chartreuse-green flowers surrounded by leaf-like bracts of the same acid-green color, which pair with nearly any other cut flower and hold their fresh color for one to two weeks in a vase. The upright, branching stems and slender blue-green foliage add a light, textural, greenery-like presence to bouquets and arrangements without competing with bolder blooms. Like many cool-season umbellifers it bolts and declines in the heat of summer, so succession sow every three to four weeks in spring for a steady cutting supply, and expect a second flush from a fall sowing in mild climates. Harvest when most of the flower clusters on a stem have opened for the longest vase life.
sources: Association of Specialty Cut Flower Growers
